title: Boulderfield
primary_metric: estimated ground-team travel time (minutes), trailhead to patient, The Keyhole Route vs. The Loft

options.B: The Loft -- the shorter, steeper, unmaintained route, 13.0 route-miles round trip with 5,300 ft of elevation gain, requiring extra route-finding time above the Boulderfield

sources.org: NOAA Storm Prediction Center (sounding/lapse-rate glossary context); standard-atmosphere meteorology

sources.note: The NWS glossary's own headline figure is the dry adiabatic lapse rate (5.5 F/1,000 ft), a different, steeper reference rate for a rising unsaturated air parcel; this case instead uses the commonly cited ~3.5 F/1,000 ft normal/environmental lapse rate (the typical observed atmospheric temperature-vs-elevation gradient), consistent with multiple independent meteorology references. Graded MEDIUM because the precise constant is a standard reference value rather than a site-specific measurement for Longs Peak on a specific date.

_ext: keys below are pipeline extensions, additive to SPEC §4
protagonist: Talia Ferro, Lead Search and Rescue Ranger, Rocky Mountain National Park -- a former backcountry wilderness EMT who has personally stopwatch-timed both of Longs Peak's main routes herself, off-duty, every season, because she trusts a number she measured herself more than a guidebook's

overview_numerals_cleared.why: Scene-setting elevation reference in the hook ("wind is moving across rock she cannot see" above 12,000 feet) -- texture establishing the alpine setting, never used as an input to any deliverable or calculation.

deliverables.text: A one-way route breakdown: for each route, the one-way distance and one-way elevation gain, showing your arithmetic, and a comparison stating which route is shorter in distance and which gains more elevation.

A Naismith's Rule time estimate for each route, evaluated from Appendix B's formula and constants before any of this case's own timing adjustments, showing every substitution step and the order of operations used.

A total adjusted time-to-patient for each route, applying the night-pace multiplier to both and The Loft's route-finding penalty to Option B only, then stating the margin between the two as a percent of the slower route's time.

A required-pace equation: using a stated turnaround-deadline assumption, write and solve an equation for the minimum average moving pace, in miles per hour, each route would require to reach the patient by that deadline, holding the case's other stated constants fixed.

A signed-number temperature and wind chill analysis: the air temperature and wind chill (each as a signed integer) at the Boulderfield and at the summit, and the integer difference between the air temperature and the wind chill at each location, showing your work.
Two original visual displays: a bar graph of each route's total adjusted time-to-patient by component, and a signed number line plotting all four D5 temperature values.

balance.argument_a: The Keyhole Route's raw Naismith estimate (4.9667 hr) is already slightly longer than The Loft's (4.8167 hr) -- it is the longer, higher-elevation-gain-per-Naismith-formula route. But it is maintained, cairned, and NPS-signed the entire way, so it carries none of The Loft's route-finding penalty. Once the shared night-pace multiplier and The Loft's +55-minute route-finding penalty are both applied, Option A finishes faster: about 387.4 minutes (6h27m) against Option B's about 430.7 minutes (7h11m) -- a 10.05% margin. A shorter route is not automatically a faster route once real terrain conditions are priced in.
balance.argument_b: The Loft is genuinely shorter (13.0 mi vs. 14.5 mi round trip) and its raw, unadjusted Naismith time is faster than the Keyhole's. Its elevation-gain-per-mile is steeper, which some SAR literature treats as a proxy for a more direct, less wasted-motion line to elevation -- and the case's own +55-minute route-finding penalty (MA2) is an author-chosen estimate, not a measured fact: at half that penalty (P5 sensitivity), The Loft is still slower but the margin drops under 4%, and a rescue team that has run The Loft recently, in daylight, with GPS waypoints pre-loaded, could plausibly beat this case's own stated penalty.
balance.margin_basis: Compare total adjusted time-to-patient (Naismith estimate x night-pace multiplier, plus The Loft's route-finding penalty) for Option A vs. Option B using Appendix A's route statistics and Appendix B's timing model.

modeling_assumptions.basis: No public figure exists for a SAR team's exact night, full-gear pace penalty versus a daytime Naismith estimate; set as a modest, round slowdown factor, applied identically to both routes.

sensitivity_note: SPEC §6: the A-vs-B time margin (10.05%) is sensitive to MA1's night-pace multiplier and, to a lesser degree, MA2's route-finding penalty -- see sensitivity_model.py FLEX = ["night_pace_multiplier", "technical_penalty_min"]. Naismith's Rule's own constants (S4) and the route distance/elevation figures (S1, S2) are deliberately excluded from FLEX -- they are cited, not assumed; P6 (data decay) is the right probe for them. A -50% perturbation on night_pace_multiplier alone pushes the margin to 20.24%, just over the 20% cap; a +50% perturbation brings it to 6.05%. A -50%/+50% perturbation on the route-finding penalty moves the margin to 3.92%/15.45% respectively. Across the full FLEX sweep the winner (Option A, the Keyhole Route) never flips -- only the margin's size moves.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: MA1's x1.3 night/full-gear pace multiplier has no public SAR-specific figure behind it; it is a documented good-faith estimate. A -50% swing on this single estimate alone pushes the margin to 20.24%, just over the SPEC §2 20% cap -- disclosed here, in Appendix D's MA1 row, and in FACILITATOR.md's sensitivity note and Q1/Q4, not eliminated.

MA2's 55-minute route-finding penalty has no public per-incident figure behind it; it is a documented good-faith estimate for an unmaintained, unmarked Class 3 route at night. A -50% swing brings the margin down to 3.92%, and a +50% swing brings it to 15.45% -- both disclosed here and in FACILITATOR.md, not eliminated. The winner never flips across this range.
